AEClinicalPictureCounts.description:
Severity-bucketed counts from the AE clinical-picture LLM component.

Counts reflect *kept* findings only (i.e. after the dedup step
suppresses subordinate findings under a decisive global mismatch).
They are derivable from the master ``Inconsistency`` list by
filtering ``source == "llm_ae_clinical_picture"`` and
``suppressed is False``, but persisted explicitly for ergonomics
and downstream symmetry with ``ClinicalDateInconsistencyCounts``.

See: llm/tasks/ae_clinical_picture.py
AEClinicalPictureCounts.title: AEClinicalPictureCounts

AEClinicalPictureStatus.description:
Assessment status for the AE clinical-picture inconsistency component.

Distinguishes "the LLM assessed the AE pictures and produced findings"
from "no LLM assessment was performed" (no LLM client configured,
trivially-matched skip, or LLM error).  Downstream code must treat
``NOT_ASSESSED`` as *no information*, not as "assessed and found no
discrepancies".

The accompanying ``reason`` string (carried alongside the status on
``PairFeatures.ae_clinical_picture_reason``) refines ``NOT_ASSESSED``
into one of: ``""`` (assessed), ``"no_llm_client"``,
``"trivially_matched"``, or ``"llm_error"``.  Reason is a string
rather than an enum so new codes can be added without enum churn.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § AE clinical-picture inconsistency
AEClinicalPictureStatus.title: AEClinicalPictureStatus

AnchorPopulation.description:
Anchor population statistics for probability estimation.

Contains three candidate population sizes and the selected anchor.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Anchor selection
AnchorPopulation.title: AnchorPopulation

AnchorType.description:
Type of anchor population selected for probability estimation.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Anchor selection
AnchorType.title: AnchorType

CaseIdentifierKind.description:
Which of a report's own case-number fields a value was read from.

Reports carry their own case numbers under three headings, and the
same identifier may be filed under different headings by different
senders — any of the three can hold a value that is in fact a
worldwide-unique identifier. ``kind`` is therefore **provenance, not
a namespace**: it records where the value came from for audit and
display, never restricting what it may match. See
:mod:`llm_dup_dev.feature_generation.explicit_link_comparison`.
CaseIdentifierKind.title: CaseIdentifierKind

ClinicalDateFindingSummary.description:
Serializable summary of a single selected clinical-date finding.

Captures the key information needed for human review without
exposing internal implementation details.
ClinicalDateFindingSummary.title: ClinicalDateFindingSummary

ClinicalDateInconsistencyCounts.description:
Severity-bucketed counts from the clinical-date inconsistency module.

See: feature_generation/clinical_date_inconsistencies.py
ClinicalDateInconsistencyCounts.title: ClinicalDateInconsistencyCounts

EvidenceSummary.description:
Diagnostic summary of shared and report-specific evidence.

Optional field for debugging and interpretability.
Does not affect the decision logic.
EvidenceSummary.title: EvidenceSummary

ExplicitLinkAssessment.description:
Pair-level explicit-link verdict with its supporting matches.

``matches`` is empty for every verdict except ``EXPLICIT_LINK``, and
carries every resolved pointer found (not just the first) so a
reviewer can see the full basis for the link.
ExplicitLinkAssessment.title: ExplicitLinkAssessment

ExplicitLinkDirection.description:
Which report carries the pointer at the other.

Both directions may fire for one pair (each report naming the
other); each is recorded as a separate
:class:`ExplicitLinkMatch`.
ExplicitLinkDirection.title: ExplicitLinkDirection

ExplicitLinkMatch.description:
One resolved pointer: a reference on one report naming the other.

``target_kind`` records which of the *target's* own case-number
fields the pointer resolved against. It is the only provenance
available — the referencing side is an untyped C.1.9 value — and it
is audit/display information, never a constraint: matching is on
``normalized_value`` alone.
ExplicitLinkMatch.title: ExplicitLinkMatch

ExplicitLinkVerdict.description:
Deterministic pair-level verdict over the two reports' case identifiers.

``NOT_ASSESSED`` distinguishes *did not look* from *looked and found
nothing*: it is emitted when neither report carries any case
identifier data at all (the loader does not supply the fields, or the
features predate them). Downstream code must treat it as no
information, never as "assessed and unlinked".
ExplicitLinkVerdict.title: ExplicitLinkVerdict

FeatureContribution.description:
Per-feature probability contribution to the composite p_joint.

Exposes the individual feature probabilities that are multiplied
together to form p_joint. Useful for debugging and method development:
understanding which features contributed how much evidence.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Rarity-based matching evidence
FeatureContribution.title: FeatureContribution

GlobalOverlapLevel.description:
Most granular shared MedDRA-hierarchy level between two AE pictures.

Used by the deterministic AE clinical-picture assessor (Step 1).
GlobalOverlapLevel.title: GlobalOverlapLevel

Inconsistency.description:
A detected inconsistency between two reports.

Carries entries from all sources: rule-based demographic/drug-set
checks and LLM-assisted AE clinical-picture findings. The optional
``source``, ``kind``, ``rationale``, ``terms``, ``cluster_label``,
``suppressed`` and ``suppressed_by`` fields support the richer
LLM-derived entries while remaining backwards-compatible defaults
for existing rule-based call sites.

Suppressed entries (``suppressed=True``) are kept in the master
list for transparency in human review but are excluded from the
severity counts that feed downstream decision logic.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Inconsistency signals
Inconsistency.title: Inconsistency

InconsistencyCounts.description:
Summary counts of inconsistencies by severity level.

These counts are merged across all inconsistency sources:
demographic (age, weight, height, sex), drug-set, clinical-date,
and narrative-derived inconsistencies.  They feed directly into
the weighted inconsistency score w_tot in the decision logic.

Decisive inconsistencies (e.g. distinct patient IDs from the
same study, or clinical-date impossibilities) contribute to
w_tot via ``w_decisive``, which is set high enough that any
decisive count always exceeds the zone tolerance.
InconsistencyCounts.title: InconsistencyCounts

InconsistencySeverity.description:
Severity levels for detected inconsistencies between reports.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Severity levels

Levels:
    minor     – small difference, weakly suggests different individuals
    moderate  – meaningful difference, weakens the duplicate hypothesis
    strong    – strongly suggests different individuals
    decisive  – forces Different classification (e.g. distinct
                patient IDs from the same study in the narratives)
InconsistencySeverity.title: InconsistencySeverity

ProbabilityEstimate.description:
Result of the collision probability computation.

``p_joint`` is the chance-match probability for a single pairwise
opportunity; ``p_match`` adjusts it for the multiplicity of the anchor
population. Both are probabilities in [0, 1] — neither is a p-value.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Rarity-based matching evidence

p_joint.description: Chance-match probability for one equivalent pairwise opportunity: the product of the per-feature p_f values.
p_joint.title: P Joint

p_match.description: P_match = 1 - (1 - p_joint)**M: the probability that at least one chance collision occurs among the M = C(N_anchor, 2) unordered report pairs in the anchor population. Drives L_match = max(0, -log10(P_match + epsilon)). A multiplicity-adjusted chance-match probability under an independence/equivalent-opportunity assumption, not a p-value.
p_match.title: P Match

ProbabilityEstimate.title: ProbabilityEstimate

ReportingContext.description:
The population context for frequency estimation.

Defines the subset of the database within which probabilities
and frequencies are evaluated.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Reporting context
ReportingContext.title: ReportingContext

ReportingContextLevel.description:
Granularity of the reporting context used for probability estimation.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Reporting context
ReportingContextLevel.title: ReportingContextLevel

RuleBasedAEClinicalPictureDetails.description:
Audit trail of the deterministic Step-1 / Step-2 AE clinical-picture
assessment. Surfaced on the result and on ``PairFeatures`` so the
review HTML and downstream tooling can display the underlying U/M
counts and overlap level alongside the bucketed severity counts.

See: feature_generation/ae_clinical_picture_rules.py
RuleBasedAEClinicalPictureDetails.title: RuleBasedAEClinicalPictureDetails

SourceCaseAssessment.description:
Pair-level deterministic result of comparing two extractions.

Produced by
:func:`llm_dup_dev.feature_generation.source_case_comparison.compare_source_case`.
No LLM is involved at this stage.

shared_source_identifier.description: Normalized shared identifier when both extractions agree on one; null otherwise.
shared_source_identifier.title: Shared Source Identifier

case_identifiers_compared.description: True when both extractions had non-null case identifiers and the comparator attempted to compare them.
case_identifiers_compared.title: Case Identifiers Compared

case_identifiers_comparable.description: True when the two case identifiers were judged safely comparable (same family, non-empty normalized values).
case_identifiers_comparable.title: Case Identifiers Comparable

reasoning.description: Short explanation of which rule fired.
reasoning.title: Reasoning

SourceCaseAssessment.title: SourceCaseAssessment

SourceCaseVerdict.description: Deterministic pair-level verdict derived from two narrative extractions.
SourceCaseVerdict.title: SourceCaseVerdict

SourceIdentifierType.description:
Kind of identifier that would link sibling reports to the same source.

``linked_case`` covers strings like ``"Linked case: AB-123456789"`` that
are expected to appear verbatim across reports sharing the same
underlying case. It is classified here as a *source* identifier, not a
*case-within-source* identifier, because its defining property is that
sibling reports carry the identical string.

``study_name``, ``trial_registration``, ``pmid``, and ``protocol_number``
cover named studies (e.g. "EpcoReal", "PARADIGM-HF"), trial-registry IDs
(NCT, EudraCT, ISRCTN), PubMed IDs, and sponsor protocol numbers. A
single narrative may carry several of these simultaneously; each is
represented as a separate :class:`SourceIdentifier` entry.
SourceIdentifierType.title: SourceIdentifierType

description:
All derived features for adjudicating a candidate duplicate report pair.

Combines shared clinical context, anchor population statistics,
rarity-based matching evidence, detected inconsistencies and
(optionally) narrative consistency. Computed from the Report layer
and statistical summaries; provides the inputs to the duplicate
adjudication decision logic.

See: docs/data_contracts.md § PairFeatures Layer
title: PairFeatures
